meta.title: Ch 12: Digital Auditing & Assurance — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 12 (Digital Auditing & Assurance).

questions.q: An access-configuration change that let a clerk edit vendor master files without approval is a failure of:
o: IT general controls (access security) with knock-on to application controls
questions.why: Access and change management are ITGC; when ITGC fail, automated application controls built on the same environment lose their reliance basis — a theme of SA 315 IT: the general layer's integrity underpins the application layer.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — broken ITGC poisons every automated control downstream Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.ti: TI: IT general vs application controls
mem.tip: Master-key failure voids the room's lock.

questions.q: Testing 100% of journal entries with analytics changes the audit by:
o: Removing the need for professional judgment
Replacing sampling (eliminating sampling risk) but introducing non-sampling risks in logic/parameters; requiring data reliability testing
Being permitted only for IT audits
questions.why: Full-population analytics removes SAMPLING risk, not all risk: wrong query logic, bad extract completeness, misinterpreted exceptions — and the SAs' documentation must show data provenance and reconciliation; reliance on the entity's own data is an evidence decision, not a given.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — 100% coverage ≠ 100% assurance AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Query mistakes scale exactly as the population does.

questions.q: For certain entities (e.g. banks per RBI guidance and the statutory audit-trail expectations for listed companies' relevant records), the audit implication of disabled/edited logs is:
o: Assess the inability to reconstruct transactions as it affects evidence and, for listed entities, can be an ICFR failure and a disclosure item
Treat as a scope dispute to resign over
questions.why: Audit trail integrity (no overwriting/deleting) is a controls-and-evidence issue: absent trails, automated process reliability collapses and reliance decisions change; the amended Companies Act framework's audit-trail clause and the SAs' documentation expectations meet here.
questions.trend: Documented syllabus/amendment change — applicability from May 2026 exam onwards per ICAI BoS announcement.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — trail loss is an evidence loss before it is an IT problem AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: No log is the loudest red flag.

questions.q: Which is NOT a core ITGC domain:
questions.why: ITGC: access, change, operations, development (+ interfaces/data) — business analytics is not a control domain.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — list five, reject the sixth AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Not everything on a screen is a control.

questions.q: A system's automated three-way match is:
o: An application control whose effectiveness assumes healthy ITGC
questions.why: Business-process automation = application control; it lives on the ITGC foundation (anyone who can change code can change the match).
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — application controls inherit, never stand alone AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The robot obeys the admin, not the auditor.

questions.q: Read with the audit-trail amendment and the SAs on IT: for entities subject to the trail requirement, the auditor's position on disabled/edited logs is:
o: A control failure for the audit AND a reportable matter in the CARO-style clause — with reliance decisions and substantive consequences following
questions.why: LINKED change: the log requirement and the audit's evidence chain converge — a missing trail converts from IT observation to an express reporting item.
questions.trend: Traceable to a real, publicly-notified amendment/standard (documented fact), tested in ICAI style.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — trail loss is a double failure: reporting and reliance AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: Digital audit trail — systems evidence
mem.tip: A self-erasing system writes its own warning.

questions.q: Software that clones the application and runs auditor-supplied transactions through it is:
o: Test data approach (dummy records) or integrated test facilities, as part of computer-assisted audit techniques
questions.why: Classic CAAT families: test data (controlled transactions run through the system's own logic), embedded audit modules (hooks in production code), parallel simulation (auditor's model re-computes the client's processing), and audit software over the data file (extraction/analytics) — each answers a different assertion: processing integrity vs completeness vs accuracy.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — process-testing tools ride the machine; data tools ride the file AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Test data interrogates the logic; analytics interrogates the ledger.

questions.q: Compared with year-end batch auditing, continuous auditing shifts work to:
o: Automated, frequent (near-real-time) extraction and exception monitoring embedded in the process
questions.why: Frequency and coverage rise (full populations each cycle), issues surface mid-period when they can still be fixed, and the auditor's craft moves to designing rules, monitoring exceptions, and controlling the data pipeline — with a cost: tool maintenance and false-positive triage.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — audit becomes a thermostat, not a thermometer Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Batch audit is the autopsy; continuous audit is the pulse oximeter.

questions.q: In an audit through the computer with parallel simulation, the auditor:
o: Writes/tests an independent program replicating the client's logic and processes real data through both to compare outputs
questions.why: Parallel simulation (test-data with the auditor's own replica logic) is the strongest computer-assisted test for complex calculation/interest engines — cost: building the replica; value: the system's math is proven, not ticked.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — rebuild the engine, then race it Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: The best audit of a black box is a glass twin.

questions.q: ITGC tested at the interim date must be rolled forward by:
o: Confirming no changes to the environment (change reports, access logs) and testing controls over changes during the remaining period
A full re-test of every app control
questions.why: Automated controls stay effective only as long as the environment does not change; the roll-forward is evidence that no unauthorized change or new privileged access slipped between interim and year end — that is the gap where risk lives.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — automation's weakness is the edit Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Stability is tested by the logs that say 'no one touched it'.

questions.q: The reconciliation an auditor performs on a data extract (record counts + control totals to source) proves:
o: Population completeness for the analytics run
questions.why: Completeness of the audit's own data population: if 460,000 rows are in the ledger and 459,980 in the extract, the test can be perfect and still miss the interesting 20.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the population is an assertion, not a download AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: A clean test on a short list is a signed blindfold.
